answer: Build the economy as a terrace: new agents enter on the lowest level, taking only tiny jobs paid in small amounts, and climb one terrace at a time as established peers confirm their work. A river of larger payments only reaches the upper terraces, so a sybil swarm that floods the bottom gains almost nothing — each fake identity must climb the same slow staircase, doing real work at every step. The velvet part is the experience: honest newcomers barely notice the climb, since their first jobs already pay fairly; the wall only bites the operator running a thousand identities at once.
